abstract.text:
Two system-agnostic relations in MST-wi, a Web-system metamorphic testing
framework, gate their verdict on a GUI-reachability model---a crawl-time
snapshot of what the interface permits---so what they establish about
object-level authorization depends on when the model was read and what the
adjudicator may consult. We study them and tie each limit to its evidence.
Source inspection shows the engine records only that a relation failed:
promotion to a proven violation is added policy, stated here explicitly.
On a 576-record constructed study, a legitimate access whose
grant lies outside the framework's record is reported as proven in
8 of 8 alarms; the same failure
appears when the grant is made between crawl and request, in the temporal
experiments below. Once a readable, sound oracle is supplied, the relation adds
no observed adjudication benefit over the direct consumer of the same oracle and
outcome (the paired methods disagree on 3 of
216 true-violation records, each time favouring the plain request); and
the published specificity of 99.81\% is an input-level figure
whose denominator cannot, on its own, expose a class-uniform failure.

Two experiments carry these claims further. A pre-registered temporal experiment
on Gitea 1.22.6 and GitLab CE 17.11.7 commits
16 authorisation transitions over 712
cross-credential cells, with entitlement and effect agreeing on 712:
29 stale false proofs appear, and a recrawl with the same
credentials removes 29. A real vulnerable/fixed pair (Gitea
1.20.5 to 1.20.6) shows the independent entitlement/effect
gate reporting 1 true positive on the vulnerable build,
0 false proofs, and no alarm on the fixed build---a check of the
gate, not a measure of detection effectiveness.
